    CMP sfx_noise_written,X         \ write's pulse works the amplitude out: A = v >> 4. What the chip has (a tone
    BEQ sfx_write.g1_rts             \ channel's slot of the noise control's array; a request left a high byte,
    STA sfx_noise_written,X         \ never 0-15): unchanged, nothing to send
    EOR g1_att_bits,X                \ the chip takes attenuation, &10: an amplitude latch byte: (n EOR &1F) OR channel
    BRA sfx_write.ddra_set_c046b    \ 65C02 opcode

    EQUB &9F, &BF, &DF, &FF         \ channel bits OR &1F
.amplitude

    LSR A
    LSR A
    LSR A
    LSR A
    EOR g1_att_bits,X
noise = sfx_write.noise             \ after sfx_write's RTS
}
    \ falls through
\ A to the chip, as MOS 3.20 writes it (&F5E6). Keeps X. The byte for the next write is worked out
\ while the write enable is low (the MOS's delay there): after sfx_write, A = a tone's high byte (from the
\ period just stepped); after ddra_set_c046b, A = the amplitude v >> 4. Meant for sfx_output's tone; other
\ callers ignore A. No wait after the write enable goes high (the MOS's LDY #4 loop, 21 cycles; the lines
\ below it are no longer reached): the next write enable falls at least 20 cycles later (a tone's low byte,
\ its high byte: an RTS, a JSR and two stores), the chip needing 32 of its 4 MHz clocks, 16 cycles.
.sfx_write
{
    LDY #&FF
    STY sysvia_ddra
    STA sysvia_ora_nh
    STZ sysvia_orb                  \ latch line 0 low: write enable
    LDA sfx_p_hi,X                  \ a tone's high byte: the period >> 4: C = bit 0 of the period's high byte,
    LSR A                           \ A = its bit 1 in bit 0 with the low byte's bits 7-4 above (the rest
    EOR sfx_p_lo,X                  \ of the low nibble is dropped below)
    AND #&01
    EOR sfx_p_lo,X
    ROR A                           \ the two bits of the high byte enter at the top and the low byte's
    ROR A                           \ high nibble comes down beside them: &00 &00 h1 h0 l7-l4
    LSR A
    LSR A
    BRA g1_fin                       \ 65C02 opcode
.ddra_set_c046b                     \ entered with DDRA already &FF (sfx_output's tone)
    STA sysvia_ora_nh
    STZ sysvia_orb                  \ latch line 0 low: write enable
    LDA sfx_v,X                     \ the amplitude, n = v >> 4
    LSR A
    LSR A
    LSR A
    LSR A
.g1_fin
    LDY #&08
    STY sysvia_orb                  \ and high again
.g1_rts
    RTS
candidates.summary: Work the next byte out while the chip's write enable is low instead of waiting there, send no wait after it goes high, send an unchanged tone amplitude not at all. sfx_write's pulse (LDY #2 loop, 11 cycles, lines 186-188 now unreachable) is replaced: the low-byte entry works the tone's high byte out of sfx_p_hi/sfx_p_lo (A on return, 24 cycles, 4 fewer than before and no AND #&3F), the ddra_set entry works v >> 4 out (A on return), and both end LDY #8 / STY orb / RTS, with no LDY #4 wait loop (lines 191-195 unreachable). sfx_output's tone is then JSR ddra_set (the high byte, already in A), CMP the cached amplitude, BEQ to sfx_write's RTS when unchanged, else cache it, EOR table, BRA ddra_set. Measured on the bench build, pcprof seed 1, 1500 passes: interrupts 1587 -> 1360 a pass (work, the wait for the flip excluded, -53), holding RIGHT 1029 -> 965 (work -22). Bank 5 grows 15 bytes (17 free). Candidates 2-4 are subsets of this one (alternatives: they overlap).
candidates.equivalence: The tone's high byte (period >> 4, bits 7-6 clear) is now made as: LDA p_hi; LSR A (C = p_hi bit 0); EOR p_lo; AND #&01; EOR p_lo (A = p_lo with bit 0 replaced by p_hi bit 1); ROR A; ROR A (p_hi bit 0 enters at bit 7, bit 1 at bit 6 after the second ROR, p_lo's high nibble moves down 2); LSR A; LSR A. Result = (p_hi AND 3) << 4 | p_lo >> 4 with bits 7-6 clear, which is exactly the old sequence's value ((p_lo AND &F0 OR p_hi AND &0F) rotated left 4, AND #&3F); checked for all 65,536 (p_lo, p_hi) pairs against the old ASL/ADC #&80/ROL sequence (no assumption about p_hi's range). 24 cycles, 16 bytes against 28, 21. The amplitude latch byte is (n EOR &1F) OR channel_bits with n = v >> 4 (0-15): n EOR (channel_bits OR &1F) is the same byte (channel_bits' low 5 bits are 0, n < 32), so one EOR from the table &9F, &BF, &DF, &FF (4 bytes, placed after the BRA/RTS, never executed) replaces EOR #&1F / ORA sfx_channel_bits,X in both the tone and the noise copies (-2 bytes each, +4 table: net 0). A tone channel's amplitude is sent only when it differs from the last one sent on that channel: the chip keeps its attenuation register, so the register file is the same after every tick. The last value is kept in sfx_noise_written,X for X = 0-2, bytes that nothing read before (only X = 3 holds the noise control) and that the request path already fills with the effect address's high byte (&A5-&A7, never 0-15) whenever a channel is given a new effect, so the first tick of every effect writes. A ramp change inside an effect leaves it alone (the chip still holds that amplitude); .ended / sfx_silence do not touch it but the channel is then idle (sfx_n = 0) until the next request, which re-marks it. The noise channel's own amplitude write is unchanged. Timing: the write-enable pulse stays 11+ cycles low (24 for the low byte's, 12 for the others: a longer low is harmless, the data stays on port A) and high-to-next-low is at least 20 cycles (tone low byte -> high byte: RTS, JSR, STA, STZ) against the MOS's 27+ and the chip's 16 cycles (32 clocks of 4 MHz); every other path is 32 or more. Callers other than the tone ignore A and Y on return (grep'd: sfx_tick never reads Y after sfx_output/sfx_next_ramp/.ended; the noise and .ended paths load A afresh), and the work done in the low phase for them (reading sfx_p_hi/sfx_p_lo/sfx_v at X = 0-3) has no side effects. Checked in the emulator on the bench build: the SN76489 register file (three periods, four attenuations, noise control) after every tick, 8 effects on each of 4 channels over 90 fields (32 runs), and seven scenarios (simultaneous effects, an effect replaced mid-way and by itself, sfx_silence mid-effect then a new one, noise, effects on the wrong channel, a burst of 40 requests) are identical to the control's tick by tick; the chip is written 20% fewer times (1,885 against 2,350 bytes in the 32 runs).
candidates.relies_on: sfx_noise_written,0-2 are written by nothing but the request path (STA sfx_noise_written,X, line 37) and read by nothing but the noise path for X = 3 (grep'd across src/ and tools/): reusing the three slots is safe only while that stays true. Every start of an effect on a tone channel goes through that request path (sfx_next_ramp is called from there and from the tick's own ramp change); nothing else writes the chip while irq_owned (the MOS's tick is off in play; the front end brackets with sfx_silence, both ways), so the cache cannot go stale. No data moves: sfx_noise_written, sfx_v, sfx_p_lo/hi keep their meaning; the new 4-byte table g1_att_bits sits after the BRA/RTS in sfx_output's scope. Bank 5 free space goes from 17 to 2 bytes (ASSERT at the end of DATA2); the code from sfx_write on (sfx_data, compiled_bank5, credits, the ANDY blob) moves up 15 bytes, and pcprof shows no hot branch or table read changing page: render phase 23,430 -> 23,408 (seed 1), 28,406 -> 28,396 (RIGHT). Inside the change every branch and loop stays in page &A5 (BEQ noise offset &67 of 127). Lines 186-195 (.wait_low .. RTS of the old tail) stay in the file but nothing reaches them. The comment at sfx_silence (ends in sfx_write: Y = 0) is now stale, Y is not read by anything. Entries: sfx_write, sfx_write.noise, sfx_output.amplitude and sfx_next_ramp.ended's BRA sfx_write keep their addresses' meaning; no `name +` entry into this window (grep'd).

candidates.summary: No timing change at all: the 24-cycle high-byte arithmetic, the EOR table, and a tone amplitude that has not changed since the last write is not sent (cache in the tone channels' sfx_noise_written slots; RTS as g4_same). sfx_write and the old tail (waits included) are untouched. Measured, bench build, pcprof seed 1: interrupts 1587 -> 1500 a pass (work -20), RIGHT 1029 -> 1004 (work -10). Bank 5 grows 4 bytes. Alternative to candidates 1, 2, 3 (overlaps).
candidates.equivalence: The tone's high byte (period >> 4, bits 7-6 clear) is now made as: LDA p_hi; LSR A (C = p_hi bit 0); EOR p_lo; AND #&01; EOR p_lo (A = p_lo with bit 0 replaced by p_hi bit 1); ROR A; ROR A (p_hi bit 0 enters at bit 7, bit 1 at bit 6 after the second ROR, p_lo's high nibble moves down 2); LSR A; LSR A. Result = (p_hi AND 3) << 4 | p_lo >> 4 with bits 7-6 clear, which is exactly the old sequence's value ((p_lo AND &F0 OR p_hi AND &0F) rotated left 4, AND #&3F); checked for all 65,536 (p_lo, p_hi) pairs against the old ASL/ADC #&80/ROL sequence (no assumption about p_hi's range). 24 cycles, 16 bytes against 28, 21. The amplitude latch byte is (n EOR &1F) OR channel_bits with n = v >> 4 (0-15): n EOR (channel_bits OR &1F) is the same byte (channel_bits' low 5 bits are 0, n < 32), so one EOR from the table &9F, &BF, &DF, &FF (4 bytes, placed after the BRA/RTS, never executed) replaces EOR #&1F / ORA sfx_channel_bits,X in both the tone and the noise copies (-2 bytes each, +4 table: net 0). A tone channel's amplitude is sent only when it differs from the last one sent on that channel: the chip keeps its attenuation register, so the register file is the same after every tick. The last value is kept in sfx_noise_written,X for X = 0-2, bytes that nothing read before (only X = 3 holds the noise control) and that the request path already fills with the effect address's high byte (&A5-&A7, never 0-15) whenever a channel is given a new effect, so the first tick of every effect writes. A ramp change inside an effect leaves it alone (the chip still holds that amplitude); .ended / sfx_silence do not touch it but the channel is then idle (sfx_n = 0) until the next request, which re-marks it. The noise channel's own amplitude write is unchanged. The chip receives the control's bytes except the amplitude latch bytes that would not change the register; its register file after every tick is identical in the 32 runs and the seven scenarios. The pulse and its waits are the control's.
candidates.relies_on: sfx_noise_written,0-2 are written by nothing but the request path (STA sfx_noise_written,X, line 37) and read by nothing but the noise path for X = 3 (grep'd across src/ and tools/): reusing the three slots is safe only while that stays true. Every start of an effect on a tone channel goes through that request path (sfx_next_ramp is called from there and from the tick's own ramp change); nothing else writes the chip while irq_owned (the MOS's tick is off in play; the front end brackets with sfx_silence, both ways), so the cache cannot go stale. Bank 5 free space 17 -> 13 bytes; code from sfx_write on moves up 4 bytes (render phase 23,430 -> 23,422 seed 1).
